## VOLUME 07 BATCH 0004 — Chapters 331–340, *Delegation*. **The live block. The block below it, `## VOLUME 07 BATCH 0003`, and everything under that, is archive and is not edited by this phase.** Chapters 1–340 are canon; `outline/series.md` outranks `outline/volume-07.md` and this file. **This is a summary and not a re-narration: one paragraph per chapter, the finding each one carries, the money where the chapter has a figure, and nothing advanced the chapter does not advance.** **THE REVIEW OF THIS BAND IS AT `logs/batch-0004.review.log` AND WHAT IT FOUND AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT IS §10 OF THE TOP BLOCK OF `state/current.md`. FOUR OF THE FIGURES IN THIS BLOCK WERE WRONG AGAINST THE CHAPTERS AND ALL FOUR ARE NOW CORRECTED IN PLACE, WITH THE CHAPTER AND LINE NAMED.**

**Chapter 331 — He Starts To Count And The Count Will Not Close.** Shelf day 206, the fourth day of the sixty-ninth week, his eighty-first morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS SECOND PARAGRAPH: there is no plank on that road, no figure on any wall in the county he is walking out of, no woman of forty-one within four days, a stroke does not travel, and the only man who could have had a figure this morning was standing at the foot of a ladder at the second light and he was not one.** His own day is four bells and nothing whatever on top of them, which is four. The man of about thirty-eight is a day and a half of a cart's going up the lane ahead of him and cannot be overtaken, and there is nobody in between, **because the whole of the transport in this country is a person going where they were going anyway.** The arrangement he most wants to carry is four days behind him and is going to stay four days behind him, and a set of beam scales and a man of seventy and a woman of about fifty-eight and a man of thirty-eight with a bag are on the other end of it and nobody can be told. Then the count, out loud, at the side of the road, on his own, and it does not close: four days up a lane, eleven miles down and off it twice, eleven miles the other way, three miles, a track of two miles, and two legs. **Carrying one prevents carrying another, and a man who decides other people can be in two of them has decided a person is a thing that can be in two places, and he has spent eighty-one mornings finding out he is one too — and then the other half, which is the half the count is for: every one of the six already has a person in it who is already doing that, and the answer is not that he carries it but that he gets out of the way, and there is no instrument that lets a man do that to somebody on purpose.** He says the price out loud to an empty lane and decides, at about the seventh hour, on his own, with no instrument, and nobody in the world knows. Nine days is the price and it is the only figure he has and no person can check it. No money. No panel.

**Chapter 332 — A Man Of Fifty-Two On A Lane, And A Sentence He Does Not Finish.** Shelf day 207, the fifth day of the sixty-ninth week, his eighty-second morning. **THE FIGURE IS SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND AND TWENTY-SIX, and he read it himself off the wall at the foot of the ladder, and he came into the March in the small hours and slept two hours in a byre.** His own day is four bells and a stranger, which is seven, and the stranger is him. Nobody has been chosen, and a woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the bottom end of the lane says so before he asks, **and she is one woman and not two; the canon split on her age is at `state/current.md` §8.14 and is for the Volume 07 close to settle,** **and the man of thirty-eight went out of that market on a cart two days ago at a quarter past seven with a book he has not decided about, and the woman with a bag carries it nine times a year and is not going to be chosen either and is right, and the woman at the bar is not going to be chosen either.** Then he goes to the gate at the near end of the lane where the man of fifty-two is counting what crosses, because a man who counts what crosses is at a place things cross, and Tarin Keel was not asked to be there and does not say so and does not offer and did not put the cart down. **THE PAST, USED ONCE: there was a gate with a levy behind it once, a levy on loads, and the loads were counted by a man who was not paid, and there is a dead man in the fourth line, and that is all he is going to say about it and you did not ask me and that is the only reason I have said it.** He stops there. **The man of thirty-one had the question ready and did not ask it, and nobody helped him and nobody noticed, and that cost him nothing, which is how he knows it was right.** Then the finding of the morning: the honest version of a fund is a wage, and a wage is a place on a day, and a place that pays a person is an office, and there is no office in this county. **And then the day turns over: there is no form in this country that says a man may put a name at the foot of a thing, and he has been using the absence of one as a reason to do nothing for eighty-two mornings, and that is a use and it is not a good one. The paper is not the difficulty. A paper with a name on it is a thing a person can be asked about for the rest of their life, and a man of fifty-two says the second half of it in nine words.** No money.

**Chapter 333 — He Tries To Carry A Book And It Comes Apart In His Hands.** Shelf day 208, the sixth day of the sixty-ninth week, his eighty-third morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS SECOND PARAGRAPH, AND IT SAYS SOMETHING THE OTHER SIX DO NOT: the market running in this street is a market in this county and it weighs four and the day is on that plank, and the wall with the day on it is nine miles up a lane, and the second light came and went where he was not.** His own day is four bells and a market, which is eight. The book is on a shelf in a room over a smithy that is a dead woman's room with the straw still in the bed in it, and the man of about thirty-four says the thing before he is asked: he cannot follow a sum that runs down a page and everybody in that village has known it since he was about fifteen. The smith's wife says hers and a woman of about forty-one comes for the water once a week and could read a column and told her four years ago she would be frightened of a book in that house at night. **Nobody answers the ordinary question in that room, and that is the finding.** Then a woman with a bag goes past in the lane with a foolscap book under her arm, going up the lane, and she does not stop, and she says one sentence to the road, and nobody sent her and she is not on his list and he is not going to ask her. **THEN HE TAKES THE BOOK OFF THE SHELF AND IT COMES APART IN HIS HANDS IN ABOUT NINE SECONDS — the mended strap first and then the stitching, done four times by four different hands — and he puts the boards down gently and says a book on a shelf is not a weight, it is an answer to a question somebody has to ask, and a stranger holding a book is a man holding somebody else's week. The man of about thirty-four says the thing that finishes it: nobody in this room believes you are going to be here in a year and you know it too and it is the one thing everybody here has got the same opinion about and it is correct.** The smith's wife puts it back at the height her grandmother had it at. He says out loud that he has to put somebody's name on something and has not got one and there is no form and **there is no sheet in this county and no scrivener within nine miles of that smithy, and he has been using the absence of a form as a reason to do nothing for eighty-three mornings and that is not a good one.** At the end of the lane the barwoman tells him one ordinary fact about that room he did not ask for and cannot use, and says the third thing she has said to him in a month that nobody asked her for, and says she is not the seventh of him and is not on the list. No money.

**Chapter 334 — A Rota With Eleven Names On It And A Twelfth In A Stranger's Hand.** Shelf day 209, the seventh and last day of the sixty-ninth week, his eighty-fourth morning. **THE FIGURE IS SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND AND FORTY-ONE, and he read it himself off the wall at the foot of the ladder.** His own day is four bells and a debt called in, which is six, and the debt was called in in this village and the boundary is four hundred yards of hedge and three miles up the lane away. The nine mornings of the walk begin at about the seventh hour tomorrow and run to the ninth, and he was going to be at a bridge with one rail on it in a valley of sixty people on the fifth of them, **and the two of those things cannot both happen and he had known that for about a month and had said it out loud in three places and had not done one single thing about it.** A debt at the ninth house, called in for the fourth time by the man who reads things out for a living, with four children behind the door and no man in the house; the door is shut; **he has a right to be at that door four times and not five, and there is no form in this country that says a man may stop being allowed to stand on a step, and there is nothing in four hundred miles that would let me.** The stranger stands off and says nothing for four minutes. Then three miles up the lane, a kitchen, nine people, a flour bill face down since Chapter 303, eleven names and a twelfth in a stranger's hand that the man of about sixty-three wrote because a stranger offered to walk a hedge and does not know he did it. **The man of sixty-three says he has walked all nine days and never once with anybody, and that six of the nine days he stood at one end of four hundred yards of hedge by himself and talked to a hedge, and that the woman who used to walk it is gone since the spring and there is a foot of that walk with nobody on it and it is still walked and nobody has noticed and he has got no way of saying it to anybody that is not a stranger.** Then he tries to carry it, in a room, in front of nine people, and it does not work, **and the reason is not a leg and not a distance: a man who carries it is a man who has to be there on nine mornings.** **AND HE SAYS THE PRICE OUT LOUD BEFORE HE ASKS, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS COUNTRY: a person who is handed a thing for a place becomes a person in a record, and there is no instrument that takes a person back out of one, and nobody in this kitchen is going to be thanked for it, and I am going to do it anyway because the alternative is that four hundred yards of hedge are walked by a man of sixty-three on his own for another year and I cannot stop that and cannot take it over.** He says it to the man and not to the room. **And the answer is neither yes nor no. The man of sixty-three puts both hands flat on the table and asks him a question: how many of the nine come in a year — not how many walk it, how many are there. And the man of thirty-one cannot answer it, in four seconds, in front of nine people, and nobody helps him, and it is the same shape of question a man of seventy asked him ten days earlier in a market town four days up the lane, and the plinth is Chapter 324, which is his seventy-fourth morning, and not the seventy-third and he could not answer that one either.** The bill stays face up and nobody turns it over and nobody reads a name out loud. No money.

**Chapter 335 — A Book That Can Order Things And Cannot Date Them.** Shelf day 210, the first day of the seventieth week, his eighty-fifth morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS FIRST PARAGRAPH: the plank is three miles down this lane and a woman of forty-one was on a ladder at the second light, and the day she put on it is not available to a man in a kitchen at the end of a lane in the third village.** His own day is four bells and a boundary, **which is eleven, and it is the only eleven in this county that is not four bells and three strangers, and the chapter that carries it is the one where a boundary is walked, and nobody in it says so.** Nine of eleven went out at about the seventh hour. He did not go with them, because a stranger standing at the north end of four hundred yards of somebody's arrangement is a man who has been added to it, and the man of about sixty-three had not been asked. They came back at the ninth hour and the man of about sixty-three said one flat thing — nine days, six of them on his own, a stranger on the seventh who said not nine words the whole way — and then **a boy of seventeen came in with his book under his arm and said the thing, and nobody had asked him and there is no form in this country that says a man may ask a boy of seventeen a question about a book.** Put them in an order and let each one say who comes next; that is the only thing anybody has proposed about the six in a month and a man who reads things out said it in a yard and nobody agreed and nobody disagreed, and it is the only thing that works, and a book can order things and cannot date them and he has never been able to make it do a date and he has stopped trying. **THE ORDER IS NOT A LIST OF PLACES. IT IS A ROUND OF TURNS, AND IT GOES ROUND, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM SAYS WHO IS AFTER THEM, AND IF A PERSON WILL NOT SAY THEN IT STOPS AT THEM AND THAT IS THE ANSWER, AND THERE IS NO OTHER ANSWER IN THIS COUNTRY.** He reads the round out and stops for about four seconds at the seventh turn: the woman of about seventy-four says a person that nobody in eleven villages has counted, and he is not going to read a name out of it because there is not one. Then, before anybody can get a word in, he says the two things he is not going to be asked about: there is a question in the book with a mark on the end of it that nobody has ever answered, and there is a third place he can see and has never been able to make out. **The man of about sixty-three opened his mouth and the boy put two fingers flat on the cover and the man shut his mouth again, and that is the only time that question came within a foot of being asked and it is still in there.** A woman of about fifty-one who cannot write then says, in nine words, that a thing that has to be held in six places at once is a hearing, and that a book is the only thing in eleven villages that can put six things in an order and the only thing that cannot say when. Nobody praised her. Nobody thanked the boy, and the man of thirty-one did not reward him because he had no way of doing it that was not a reward. No money.

**Chapter 336 — A Thing That Stops When The Ninth Stops, And He Is Not The Ninth.** Shelf day 211, the second day of the seventieth week, his eighty-sixth morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS FIRST PARAGRAPH: there is no plank in this hamlet and no woman of forty-one and no wall with a number on it, and he was on a rise behind eleven houses at the second light; and four bells is the one number on that plank that does not belong to a county.** His own day is four bells and nothing whatever on top of them, which is four. He comes for one thing and gets to the near gate at about the eighth hour and **there is nobody in the field, because there has not been a wet morning in this month and the last one was the last morning of the sixty-eighth week, which is Chapter 327 and his seventy-seventh morning, and the man of about seventy-four in that house went out for the first time in about a year on it and came back in before the light went. **THE DELIVERED VERSION OF THIS LINE SAID *the eleventh morning of the sixty-seventh week*, WHICH IS A DAY THAT CANNOT EXIST.** He tries it, in the open, honestly: he stands the way the man in the second house stands, for nine minutes — `336:23` — and **the phrase *the length of a load going over* is Chapter 330's, at `330:29`, and is not in this chapter, which five state files had it in,** and **nothing happened — not a refusal, not a door, not a form, not a look from a window. The field did not know. A thing kept alive by nine people turning up in the rain cannot be carried by the eleventh person who turns up because he decided to, on a dry morning, in a hat.** The woman of thirty tells him from her own step that there is nothing there to say no to, **and that if he had come in the wet there would have been nine of them and he would have been the tenth and she would have said four words at him and he would have gone, and instead he came on a dry morning and there is nobody to say anything.** The man of about fifty-one with a spade says he is right on the facts and has been since the spring and that **being right on the facts is not a thing you can carry across a gate** and that there is a man of about seventy-four in that house who does the most when it rains and is entitled to stop and that he is not going to be the man who tells a stranger that a thing he is seventy-four in cannot be asked about his own field. **A THING CANNOT BE DELEGATED TO A STRANGER**, and the fourth thing he has learned — a word is not a person, a name is not a person, a book is not a person, and now a stranger with a leg is not a person either. He said he was sorry about the wet corner and she said nine words and **the ninth of them is the same word she has been using since Chapter 307, and the word is *mine*.** No money.

**Chapter 337 — The Tenth Person Is Found By A Person Of That Place And Not By Him.** Shelf day 212, the third day of the seventieth week, his eighty-seventh morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS FIRST PARAGRAPH: the wall with the day on it is a lane away and a woman of forty-one was on a ladder against it at the second light and he was a mile off on a road with nine houses on it and could not have got to the foot of it with a leg.** His own day is four bells and a stranger, which is seven, **and the stranger is a woman of about forty-one at the seventh house and not him, and it is the ninth day in a row that the day has had a stranger in it that is not him, and he noted that in about four seconds and made nothing of it.** The road is a mile, nine householders, ninety years, each a length, unpaid, and the man of thirty is the third of the nine and has been for eleven years. He says the thing he has been waiting to say to the stranger since the fifth morning of the sixty-seventh week, which is Chapter 318 and is nineteen days back: **you said there was a tenth in this lane in front of my gate, and I stopped you, and I was right to, and I have not found one thing wrong with stopping you and have not found one thing right with saying it either, and a tenth is a count and a count is a list and a list is the thing that comes before a bill.** And the stranger says he has not got the other half, and the man of thirty asks for the bit about the field, and the stranger gives it: a boy of seventeen with a book that can order things and cannot say when, a woman of fifty-eight who said no in nine words and was right, and a field he stood in on a dry morning and was not one of. **THAT IS HOW HE FOUND OUT THAT THE COUNT ALMOST HAPPENED IN THIS LANE BECAUSE OF HIM, AND THAT A WOMAN AT THE SEVENTH HOUSE HEARD HIM SAY IT FROM A GATE AND SAID NOTHING AND WENT BACK IN, AND THAT SHE HAS BEEN DOING TWO LENGTHS IN THE DARK EVER SINCE AND WAS DOING TWO LENGTHS IN THE DARK BEFORE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NINETEEN DAYS AND ELEVEN WORDS.** Then the tenth person is found, by the man who reads things out for a living, **on his own account, because he was going that way and had not got to where he was going**, and what she tells him is a widow at the fourth house with a bad hip who had the barrow for nine years and put it down in the spring and told nobody. Asked the ordinary question at her gate, she says: it is not for anything, **it is for a hip**, and there is no form in this country that says a man may put a barrow down; she has not stopped, she is not going to, she did not start, she cannot now say no, and nobody put her on the road, and a stranger with a bad leg does not know her name and neither of them is going to find out. Then the finding and the difference from the price he has said five times: **this is not a person finding out about themselves, it is a person finding out about somebody else because of me, and there is a widow at the fourth house who will find out in about a year, and a man of thirty who has been standing in a lane for nineteen days with a thing he cannot put down either, and none of the three is going to be thanked and two of them cannot get out of it.** And at the last of the light he decides, out loud, knowing it is wrong four seconds before he says it, to put a sentence into this county about the man of thirty-eight and a column and a levy, **and is told in a lane that a sentence put into a lane is a delegation he has not authorised and cannot call back, and that he is about to do it to a woman at a bar who has been asked two questions in twenty-two years and this is the third, and that he is not going to do it because it is the right thing but because the man of thirty-eight is four days up a road and the ninety are on a list and he is on a mile of road with a leg and a fortnight.** No money.

**Chapter 338 — He Does It On Purpose And He Says The Price Out Loud. THE BAND'S CENTRE AND THE PEAK THE BAND NAMED BEFORE IT WROTE.** Shelf day 213, the fourth day of the seventieth week, his eighty-eighth morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS FIRST PARAGRAPH: the wall with the day on it is eleven miles up a lane and off it, and the second light found a woman of forty-one on a ladder against it and a man of thirty-one on a road with nine houses on it and a leg.** His own day is four bells and a market and a debt called in, which is ten, **and the chapter's second paragraph says in its own words that the market and the debt in that weight are BOTH FOUR DAYS UP THIS LANE in a county no living person has stood in, that neither is on any plank in this county, that there is a market running in the street he is standing in and a debt being called in four hundred yards behind him and that both of those are in this county and on a wall eleven miles away, and that a day carries one of each.** He does not go to the market town. There is no road that would put him in that yard and no form that says a man may be in two places and no form that says a man may send anybody. **So he does the only thing there is to do, in a lane behind a bar, and he says the whole price out loud before he asks, in about a minute, to one person: a person who carries a sentence for a place becomes a person in a record, and there is nothing in this country and nothing in any county four hundred miles off that will lift a person back out of one, and he has known that since a kitchen three miles up a lane and has had eighty-eight mornings to do something about it and has not; you will be a person who said it and not a person who was asked, paid or sent for, and there is no form that lets a man ask you whether you will do it because asking is a form, so he is not going to ask, and you will not be thanked by anybody including her; and the second half, which is the half he has no better way of putting — you cannot say no, because I have come eleven miles with nothing to offer and I have used that, and I have known what I was doing for a week and I did it anyway.** She picks her board up, turns it over and puts it down again, and says nobody has ever said that to her before, and then she says the word *go on*. He asks her to carry one sentence to a person of another place, and says it out loud first, and it is wrong in two places and he says it anyway: **he had left out the woman of about sixty-one and the man on the plinth, and a sentence about a yard that does not contain the person whose yard it is can be said in a market street to anybody and about anybody.** Then **she says it in her own mouth and it is shorter and it is worse, and it has the water in it that a stranger would not have said, and it took her eleven seconds and she did not look at him once, and she says she has never been anywhere near that town and has known all of it for a week from a bar.** He had nothing, and she had taken what he was carrying and put two of her own hands on it and it was heavier. **And then she says the part he had not priced: she is going to say it at the cross, at about the second hour, because that is where the people are, and not in a yard — because there is no yard in that town a woman of sixty-one would not hear it in twice, and there is a woman of twenty-nine at a cross there who keeps a list and has never been asked what she keeps, and she is not going to pretend to her that she has come down a lane for a private word in a yard, and she does not know a private word from a market morning and neither does anybody in this county.** Nine loads went over a weighbridge and nobody in that lane heard them. And the close: the price was said out loud before the doing and it did not make it smaller, and saying it out loud did not make it smaller; **she is a person in a record now, and there is no form anywhere in four hundred miles that will let him lift her out of it, and she did not agree to it and cannot say no and is not going to be thanked; and he is going to cost a man of about thirty-eight a second thing, and nobody has asked him whether he wants his own sentence carried, and that man is four days up a road with a bag and a bad back and no standing in nine counties and there is no instrument in four hundred miles that will tell him.** No money. No slip figure. No name of the man on the plinth.

**Chapter 339 — A Bridge With One Rail On It, And A Record He Cannot Get Her Out Of.** Shelf day 214, the fifth day of the seventieth week, his eighty-ninth morning. **NO FIGURE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS WHY IN ITS FIRST PARAGRAPH: there is no plank in a valley of sixty people two miles off a track off a lane and never has been, and the plank is a day away at the far end of the lane with a leg on it.** His own day is four bells and nothing whatever on top of them, which is four. He came up the lane in the dark and up a track of two miles and had a leg and nine days of walking in him, and he had said out loud on the eightieth morning that he was going to be here, and he had written it down nowhere. She comes down the lane at the seventh hour, stops twice, does not stop a third time, and knows him by the leg. **She says he is early and it is the second time in eighteen days and that she is not going to say it twice, and this is not the same. THEN SHE ASKS HIM A QUESTION AND IT IS NOT THE ORDINARY ONE: whose name is on it.** He has four seconds and she lets him have all four. **She says it to him about herself: there is no form in this country that says a man may put a name at the foot of a thing, there is no form, and therefore every name in this country has been put there by somebody who decided to, and a stranger with a leg has decided more of them than anybody in this valley has in forty years, and she is seventy-four and has been the instrument for about forty years and nobody has ever asked her whether she would rather not be.** And then he tells her, because she asked and because there is nowhere else to say it and because he said in six places in thirteen days that he was going to delegate one of the six on purpose: **a woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the end of a village eleven miles down the lane and off it, twenty-two years, about nine loads a day, the only board in eleven villages with a word at the top of it; he has asked her two questions in a month and both cost her something; this morning he asked her for a third and said the price out loud before he asked, and the price is that she becomes a person who said a thing and there is no instrument that takes a person out of a record; and she cannot say no and he used that and he had known what he was doing for a week.** He then says the part he had not priced and she had: **she is going to say it at a cross, in the open, at about the second hour, because that is where the people are, and not in a yard, and it is the worst thing that has happened in this country in thirteen days and he did it and cannot undo it and would do it again and has not got a better sentence for that either.** He tells her the rest: a woman of about sixty-one in that town has a foolscap book on a shelf in her own back room with a slip in it and has never been asked what it is for and said in her own yard that she is not going to be the person who says the water stops, **and in about four days a stranger's voice is going to come into that yard in a sentence out of a woman's mouth and she is not going to know where it came from, and that is the whole of the finding, and he has been on the other side of it once, in a kitchen three miles up a lane, and he stood at a gate and said not one word for an hour.** Nobody thanked him, nobody was relieved, there is nothing in this country that will take her out of a record, and he has been looking for one for eighty-nine mornings. **Then she says the thing about the porch in a different shape from the two other times: a board with eleven names on it and no date and no column and no heading and no mark, in a porch since before her mother was born, and she goes down about four mornings a year and has not been in about a month. And she says the finding he has been carrying about a lane for eighteen days and is not going to concede it, and says out loud that she is not going to concede it and that he is not going to be able to settle it, and that if she stops in the spring then it stops in the spring and nobody in this valley will do anything about it and that will be correct — and that it is not fair to the valley, and it is fair to her, and she is not going to give that up to a stranger with a leg who is going to be somewhere else in nine days.** He said nothing, did not go to the porch, did not look at the board, and went back up the track. No money.

**Chapter 340 — The Ninetieth Morning Is A Third One And Nothing Is Built On It.** Shelf day 215, the sixth day of the seventieth week, **his ninetieth morning, AND IT IS A ROUND NUMBER AND NOBODY NOTICES IT: not the man of thirty, not the man of thirty-four, not a person at a bar, nobody. Four people were in the lane at the second light and not one of them looked at the wall, and the chapter does not return to it, and no doorframe, milestone, sum, number of strokes and no number of people lands on it.** The figure is **sixty-four thousand and eighty-three**, read by him off the wall at the foot of the ladder. His own day is four bells and a market, which is eight, **and there is a market on the green by that tower this morning in this county and there is a bell in that tower that has not been rung for want of a wage and it was not rung this morning either.** He sets out for the sixth of the six and it is not the one he expected: he has been in five of them in thirteen days and the sixth is a woman of about fifty-eight at a set of beam scales four days up the lane, six months gone with a child, whose father is seventy, and who said no to him in nine words on the sixty-fourth morning and was right; on the eighty-eighth morning he decided to go and tell her a figure and on the eightieth he decided not to, and on the eighty-ninth at a bridge he was told a man cannot be in two places, **and the sixth is four days up this lane, so he walks the two miles to the nearest of the six instead, the mile of road nine men keep, and there is nobody on the length and the third house is shut and there is nothing to hand a sentence to, and he stands at the top gate a while and comes back to the green. THE DELIVERED CHAPTER HAD HIM WORK IT OUT AND STAY PUT AND THIS FILE RECORDED THE TRIP AS HAVING HAPPENED, WHICH WAS THE FALSE CLAIM THE REVIEW FOUND; THE MOVEMENT IS THE CARD'S AND IT IS IN THE CHAPTER NOW.** Then **the man of about thirty with a cart and a beast comes up the lane to the market because a market on the green is where a man with a beast stops, and says one sentence and it is not about the stranger: on the sixth morning of the seventieth week, at about the second hour, which is that morning, a woman of about thirty-four at a bar at the end of the road said a thing in the open at a cross about a town four days up this lane, and he has had it six hours, and she had it the morning before and did not say it because there were not nine of them at that cross until this morning, and a sentence put into a lane gets in front of the person who put it in there, and the stranger is eleven miles off and he is nine, and a man came through on that same morning and did not get to where he was going, and the stranger is going to be asked about it at a bar, and the bar is going to be the place he is asked about it in, and there is no form in this country that says a man may be asked about a thing in a place that is not a room. A man of about thirty-four says there is no form that says a man may stop, which is true and was not asked for and made the room worse. She says afterwards, unasked, that he is not a villain and is not going to be redeemed and is going to say the same thing at his own hearth inside a month and half of those nine will be stood in front of him again. End: **nobody has been chosen to hold the book and the chapter says who is not going to be chosen and why**, and the woman with the bag is on the list, and the reason is that a book held by somebody the village has not chosen is a book the village cannot ask anybody about, and it is the same hole that is in the floor of everything else. The day in words: sixty-third morning, seventh and last day of the sixty-sixth week. No panel, no bold.

**Chapter 314 — A Debt Called In At The Ninth House.** Shelf day 189, the first day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-fourth morning. The plank at the second light is **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and fifteen**, and he is at the foot of the ladder while she puts it there, and the day it stood for was four bells and a debt called in. **The debt was carried in at the bar the previous afternoon by a man of about twenty with a scythe who said nine words, answered none of the four questions asked of him, and went back down the lane, and about nine people in that yard heard them, and four of them worked out in about four seconds why a man with a bad leg exists in the mind of the woman of forty-one at all, and neither group said anything, and that was correct.** Nobody in Coldharrow pays a debt on the day it is called in and that is not a rule and there is no form for it. He knocks at the ninth house and nobody comes to the door, which is not the same as nobody being in. **The seam, out of a thing: a debt stops being two people in a kitchen and starts being about nine other people's estimate of the two of them, and the estimate is worth more than the money, and the money is two on a plank.** At the second light **the woman of forty-one told him, unasked, that a day's figure is a weighted number and cannot be turned back into what was done, and she named the seven weights in one sentence — *four bells is four, and a stranger is three, and a market is four, and a boundary is seven, and a debt called in is two, and a fire is two, and a burial is one* — and gave three different sixes that are all six and none of which contains a burial, and said nobody has ever asked her to, and that she is the one person in two hundred and ten who has the seven weights and that seven weights is not a day. SHE ALSO PROMISED HIM THE RIGHT QUESTION AND THEN ASKED IT, which the review of 27 September 2026 found she had not done: *you are asking me the wrong question. The right one is what a stroke is for.* **EVERY ONE OF THE BAND'S TEN OWN DAYS IS NOW DERIVABLE FROM THAT ONE SENTENCE AND A READER CAN CHECK ALL TEN, WHICH NO CHAPTER IN EITHER VOLUME 07 BAND COULD DO BEFORE.** The same morning, eleven miles off, **a woman of about thirty is told by her mother that her mother's brother, about seventy-four, fell in his own yard in the wet on the last day of the sixty-sixth week**, and she says *then it is the man with the spade*, and he has never been in the line and got in on a wet day a hundred and forty years ago, and it is the identical wet day. **THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE BAND'S SUBJECT SAID OUT LOUD BY A NARRATOR ONCE, ON PURPOSE, BECAUSE A CARD ASKED FOR IT: two things set side by side is not a room, and a reader is not a room, and a page is the only room this country has, and it is a worse instrument than a yard, and the whole of the difference is that in a yard somebody has to be in it.** End: at the bottom end of the lane of nine householders, the man of about fifty-one with a spade asks the man of about thirty with the cart whether he would take one length for money if somebody paid for it, and gets no in nine words, and goes back to his ditch, and neither of them knows that a man with a bad leg said anything about it in a kitchen eleven miles up the lane. The man of fifty-two is on the lane and is not asked what he was the only person in. Nobody thanked him and nobody told him. No money. The day in words: sixty-fourth morning, first day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold.

**Chapter 315 — A Burial At Coldharrow.** Shelf day 190, the second day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-fifth morning. The plank at the second light is **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and twenty-one**, and the day it stood for was four bells and a burial, which is five and does not happen very often. **A man of about sixty-eight who kept a barrow died three days before and was buried before the last bell, and nobody in the village could tell a stranger what he did, and he is the ninth commonest thing in Coldharrow, and he is on nobody's list in either direction.** The hole is in the corner of the chapel yard behind the last of the good ground and the man digging it is a man of about forty-four who does that for the parish out of a box and takes what is in the box. Nine people are in the yard, including the dead man's son, a man of about thirty-four who has come nine miles and has not spoken, and a woman of about sixty who lives in the sixth house and has come about a dog, and a man of about twenty with a scythe who has been at the far end of the ground since the second hour. **NOTHING IS BEING ASKED OF ANYBODY ALL DAY, WHICH IS THE CHAPTER'S REASON FOR EXISTING.** The woman of forty-one put a stroke on the plank for the burial at about the seventh hour **and cannot show anybody which stroke it was, and he wanted to ask her badly enough that he got nine feet toward her and then thought better of it, because asking her would spend the only useful thing anybody has ever got out of her on a stroke.** **THE BEAT, AND IT IS THE BEST THING IN THE BAND: the woman of about sixty asks the man of about thirty-four a question that has nothing to do with any of the six — *will you keep his dog* — and he says thank you first and then no, in about nine words, and the answer is that the dog has one place and he does not, and a dog with one place is the best thing there is, and she says then I will leave him be, and then she asks him to put his father in the corner by the wall and not out in the middle, and he says yes, aunt, and that is the whole of it.** End: the woman of forty-one says the dead man's name at the graveside in about four seconds because nobody else in that yard is going to, and nobody asked her to, and afterwards she goes up the ladder and puts the cloth over her shoulder and goes to do her day, and there is no way on that plank to tell which stroke was the burial, and he did not ask her. **No money in this chapter and the money of a burial ground is that there is none.** The day in words: sixty-fifth morning, second day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold, and the band does not resolve the fact that a plank cannot be asked what a stroke was for, because that fact is not this band's to resolve.

**Chapter 316 — A Fire In The Market Town.** Shelf day 191, the third day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-sixth morning, **and there is no plank at the end of this street and no figure on any wall at the second light and nobody in that market town has ever heard of a board at Coldharrow, and the chapter says so in its second and fifth sentences and a stroke does not travel.** **The day it belonged to came to four bells and a fire and a debt called in, and a fire in a market four days up a lane is not a March weight and is not on that plank, and the debt is in a village he has not been in since the morning before last, and he is standing in the middle of the one of those two things and he will hear about the other one never.** A yard behind a row of carts goes up at about the fourth hour and is out before the water comes and it took nine minutes. **There is no bell in that town that anybody rings for anything, and a man from another county notices it in four seconds, and the device is not restaged: nobody rings anything.** Nine people were standing at the bridge and the whole market knew inside four minutes and nobody had to tell anybody anything. Four hundred loads went over that bridge in a hurry. **THE DAY THE SECOND READER TURNED OUT TO HAVE BEEN NEEDED, AND NOBODY WAS THERE: the man of about seventy, who has kept the bridge about forty-four years and has not done the sums for about nine years, went in at the last of the light and did the column himself with a pencil, and he is right nine times in ten and on that night he was right about seven times in ten, and his daughter is six months gone with a child and was asleep at the second hour and was not woken, and there is nobody else in that town who can follow a column that runs down a page, and there is no wage for a second reader at a set of beam scales in this country and there has never been one, and that is not a scandal, it is a market.** The father of seventy then tells the man of thirty-one, in a street, standing nine feet off, the one sentence he has been holding for a week: a man of about thirty-eight came through in the spring with a cart and a book, did not go over the bridge, and asked him what his daughter is paid. **THE DECISION: he had one thing to say about this place and he does not say it, and the reason is that a woman of fifty-eight told him no in nine words eleven days ago and the no was right, and he has been in this county sixty-six days and has not found one word that makes the no less correct, and a man of seventy is going to find out tonight what it is like to be the only reader in a market at seventy at one o'clock in the morning, and the man of thirty-one is not going to be in that room, and the reason is not manners.** **The seam: where the arrangement stops being a father's trade and starts being a daughter's, and he cannot say what either side of it is for.** The people of that town call the two of them on a market morning an anchor, and an anchor is not a thing, it is the plinth, and the day, and the two of them, and there is nothing to find. The man of fifty-two is at that market three days running and says one true sentence in a yard and is asked nothing. **No money at all in this chapter, and the absence is the chapter.** The day in words: sixty-sixth morning, third day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold.

**Chapter 317 — A Rain In The Hamlet, And A Man Of About Fifty-One Who Is Right.** Shelf day 192, the fourth day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-seventh morning. The plank at the second light is **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and thirty-four**, and he was not in Coldharrow and had been told it, and the day it stood for was four bells and a stranger and a stranger, and one of the strangers was a carter's boy who came up the lane with a load for a house in the second village and went on, and nobody in Coldharrow knows his name and nobody asked. **GOAL, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS THE LAST TIME: who digs the first hole. AND NOBODY CAN SAY, AND THAT IS A GAP IN AN ARRANGEMENT AND NOT A LIE, and it took two hours to find out and almost nobody in that field thought it was strange.** The ground is deeper on the side the family came in from; the near gate is the low end; the first hole anybody can point at is at the near gate and there is nothing under it and no marker and nothing at the foot of it. The ninth did not dig it, the eighth did not dig it and is sixty-eight and well and standing in her own doorway in the rain watching a stranger ask about her field, the tenth is not born, and the man of about seventy-four who got into the line on a wet day a hundred and forty years ago did not dig it either and is in his own house and has not been out of it since the last day of the sixty-sixth week. **THE BEST SENTENCE IN THE BAND, IN THE MOUTH OF A MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE WHO IS RIGHT AND IS STILL RIGHT AND IS NOT BEING CRUEL: *The ground was like that when the family came to it.* The family came in at the near gate and the near gate is at the soft end and it is a soft place to get in at, and four hundred years of a family going in at the same soft place has put a slope on that field that you could set a water butt on, and nobody can say who dug first because there was no first, and that is not a mystery and it is not a lie and it is not anybody's fault.** **SHE ASKS HIM A QUESTION BACK, which nobody in that field had noticed until that morning except one person: *Then how do I stop* — and he does not pretend not to know, and he refuses to hand her the comfortable version because she had it off him once and he was wrong, and he tells her that a line does not have an end in it, and that nobody in this field has ever chosen where to put a hole, and that every hole in that ground is where the last hole made it easy to stand, and that he has never been in the line and got in on a wet day by shifting more earth than the next one.** End: **she says what she wants for the second time in a week and it is not longer, and then she says the other half of it once because nobody has heard her say the first half twice: *I do not want out of it. I want it to be mine.* I want to be the one who decides where the next hole goes and I want somebody to write that down somewhere, and I am not asking him to do it and I am not asking you, and I have not got anybody to ask.** Nobody is going to grant it and nobody is going to say it cannot be granted. **There is no money in any of it, and the money of a burying ground is that there is none, and a price is what you would put on it if a person were being paid, and nobody in that field is being paid and the whole of the arrangement is nine people turning up in the rain.** A boy of about eleven dug two of the holes and nobody stopped him and nobody counted the boy. The day in words: sixty-seventh morning, fourth day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold, and nothing in this chapter is a lie and nobody guessed that anything of the kind was going on.

**Chapter 318 — A Mile Of Road, And The Sum Is Still Not Written Down.** Shelf day 193, the fifth day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-eighth morning. The plank at the second light is **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and forty-four**, read by him himself, and the day it stood for was **four bells and nothing at all, which is the number a road is usually run on.** He comes up the lane from the hamlet with four days of walking in him and one fact from a market town four days up the other way: a man of fifty-two stood in a market street, watched four hundred loads go over a bridge in a hurry, said one true sentence about a gate, and was asked nothing at all. **THE COST OF PAYING THE MILE, MADE SPECIFIC AND NOT ARGUED ABOUT, IN THE MOUTH OF THE MAN OF THIRTY: a man in a tavern in the ninth year of his father's time, at the end of that lane, not a stranger, a decent man, is not a villain, it is not anybody's fault — he said he would pay for the road and paid for two years out of his own pocket at the bar in front of anybody who cared to look, and nine men mowed for him for two years and were proud of the road for the first time in seventy years, and in the third year he took a farm four miles off with a boy on it, and they had all been standing in a lane for a man for two years and not one of them had said so out loud, and nobody could look at anybody, and it took four years to get back to what they had, and one of those years was done at four men.** The man of fifty-two stands in the road for an hour and says one word and is not thanked and does not know he is paying the price. **The money, and it is the hardest thing in the card: a carter's day is eighteen pence, in two mouths, and the keeper's day is nine a day, and NOBODY DOES THE SUM, and the man of thirty says it flatly that if the two prices are ever in the same breath then somebody is doing a sum and a number in a hand is a thing a person can be entered against, and the chapter prints the two prices and not the product.** **The seam, the sixth in the band: the join is at the first gate, a hundred yards or so in, where a favour becomes a duty, and it is the same join as the fund and the scales and the line, and seeing it does not tell him what to do — and the bad thought he has before he knows it is a bad one is *the only way to stop a thing stopping is to put a person in it on purpose, and the only way to do that is to have a place where you write the name*, and the only time that instrument has ever worked in this county in living memory is a man of this family putting a spade in a hole in a wet afternoon a hundred and forty years ago and consulting nobody.** End: **A TENTH PERSON IS ALREADY ON THE ROAD AND WAS NEVER ASKED.** Barrow marks in the wet going in at the second gate, forty yards of the second house's length taken up and filled in, and the second house is a widow of sixty-eight with a bad hip. **He said *there is a tenth* in a lane, and it was the wrong thing and he knew it in four seconds and after he had said it, and the man of thirty stopped him in nine words: a tenth is a count, and a count is a list, and a list is what comes before a bill, and putting her in a place where being found out is worse than being short is not a repair.** The tenth person is a woman of about forty-one at the seventh house who did it at about the fifth hour on eleven days over eleven days and did not tell anybody and did not do it in front of anybody and cannot now say no, and the road is still nine men and the rain will take the marks out by the end of the week. The day in words: sixty-eighth morning, fifth day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold, no product.

**Chapter 319 — Six Rooms, And A Thing That Cannot Be Produced.** Shelf day 194, the sixth day of the sixty-seventh week, his sixty-ninth morning. The plank at the second light is **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and forty-eight**, and the man of about thirty-eight said it out loud in a lane at about the seventh hour, having been at the foot of the ladder at the second light, and the day that figure stood for was four bells and a stranger, and the woman of about fifty at the bar read him off her own board in four seconds and did not ask his business. **He got nine people into a yard in Coldharrow at about the ninth hour, which is the only thing this country has worth the name of a room, and nobody sent for anybody.** **THE MECHANISM, THE VOLUME'S ONE NOTCH, WRITTEN DOWN AT THE MOMENT IT IS FIRST USED, IN THE FICTION, IN A MAN'S MOUTH, IN NINE SECONDS, IN FRONT OF NINE PEOPLE WHO HAVE TO BE TOLD: *A document is a thing you produce. A hearing is a thing you have to carry. A sheet can be put in front of a room on a day. A hearing cannot be produced at all, and it is not a bad thing that cannot be produced, it is a hearing, and the only way one exists is if six people who have never met each other agree to be in it.*** **It fails on the paper, and it fails on something true: the man of about thirty-eight says there is no sheet, and a man of about twenty with a scythe says *write it on the back of a bill*, and the yard is asked *whose bill*, and goes quiet for four seconds, because the only writing paper of any kind in Coldharrow is the back of a flour bill in a kitchen three miles up the lane with eleven names on it and a twelfth in a stranger's hand, and nobody said that out loud and four people worked it out in four seconds. A copy is three pence at Sallowby and a scrivener is a penny a page, and there is neither in this county; and a copy in a place where nobody has read it is a piece of paper, and a copy in a place where somebody has read it is a place somebody can be asked, and the difference between the two is nine days of a cart.** It fails on him, in the plainest sentence available, which he has said in a field and says again in a yard and then says to one person in Chapter 320, and twice is not an ask. **THE SIX ARE NAMED OUT LOUD IN A YARD IN ABOUT FOUR MINUTES AND HE JOINS NONE OF THEM, and the woman of fifty-eight is named as not being asked for anything today or this month, and he is not going to be in it. THE SIX ARE THE SIX OF CHAPTER 311 AND THE REVIEW OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 HAD TO FIX THE LIST TO MAKE THEM SO: the woman of thirty at the end of the line of nine diggers is IN and the woman of about thirty-four at the bar is OUT, and she is now out on the page, in the chapter's own words, as not one of the six and not on the list and one for which there is no arrangement in this county. The man of thirty with the cart is now named as *whom a woman at a bar has called out loud in a lane a man who wants paying, and who told her in nine words that she was half right*, which is a report and not a fact about him, and he refuses payment three times in this batch.** The instrument that carries it: the woman of about thirty-four at the bar asked the man of thirty-eight a question in a room and he answered it, and he has stated that four times and it is true, and the man of thirty-eight asked her. **THE TIME WAS AGREED AND CHANGED TWICE — once for a move and nine days of travel, once because a woman of fifty-eight is six months gone and will be stood up at the spring, and once because the woman of about thirty said out loud in a gateway in the rain that you cannot fix a day for it, because if somebody in that hamlet dies on it then somebody in that hamlet is standing in a field and not in a room, and so take a week and do not ask her to be there, because she will be there and will not be able to say that she came — AND THEN THE PERSON OF A PLACE PROPOSED THE ONLY THING THAT COULD ACTUALLY WORK: do not settle a day, settle an order, and let each one of them say who comes next, and the day is the day of whichever one is doing the asking that week, and that is a market, and it works on a market morning and it works when nobody is standing about.** Bram Orren is there and says his one thing and does not open his book. The man of fifty-two stands at the gate for an hour and is not asked. **End: he says out loud that he is not going to be in it, and there are six people who have agreed to be somewhere on a day, and he is not one of them, and there is no form in this country that says a man may be in two places, and he has been sixty-nine days in this county and has not found one and is not going to.** The woman of forty-one says *nobody is thanked, and nobody is relieved, and I would like it noticed that this is the fifth morning this week that nobody has been relieved about anything.* The day in words: sixty-ninth morning, sixth day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold, no product.

**Chapter 320 — What The Six Said About Each Other.** Shelf day 195, the seventh and last day of the sixty-seventh week, **his seventieth morning, and it is a round number, and the man of about thirty-eight says it out loud from the bottom of the ladder at Coldharrow before the woman of forty-one has put anything on the wall, and the man of thirty-one refuses it in nine words — *it is a count of mornings, and mornings are not a day* — and neither of them is right and both of them are right, and the chapter does not return to it and no coincidence is built on it.** The plank said **sixty-three thousand nine hundred and fifty-five** at the second light, brought about the second hour by the man of thirty-eight, who brings it about four times a week, and the day it stood for was four bells and nothing at all. He comes eleven miles down and off the lane to the tenth village, and it is nine days since he said six arrangements out loud in a kitchen in Ashgill and it is ten mornings, and he had intended to go down a lane to a porch and instead he came here and cannot say why. The room over the smithy has four people in it and no market on. **THE MAN OF THIRTY-EIGHT STARTS BY CORRECTING HIMSELF OUT LOUD: he told the wrong story twice this month, a woman at that bar asked him one question in front of about nine people on a market morning and he answered it and did not say so, and somebody in that room should have known a week ago and did not, and it is not the smith's wife's fault.** Then he gives the three other threads and **none of them came from him: a man of sixty-three came to that bar nine days ago about a market and came back two days ago and asked whether there is anybody in this county who pays a person to stand still, and she did not tell him that a man of about thirty-eight had been asked the same question in the spring by a man with a book, and he does not know that; a man of about thirty with a cart and a beast came down that lane two days ago with a load and asked her the same question and did not know that a man of sixty-three had asked it earlier in the same week; and a man of about seventy in a market street four days up the other lane four days ago told a stranger about a man with a book who would not go over a bridge, and he does not know the name and could not pronounce it if he had it.** **THE BAND'S FINDING, IN THE MOUTH OF A PERSON OF A PLACE: nobody in that room had put the six beside each other, and in nine days a man of sixty-three in a village and a man of thirty in a lane have both asked the same question at the same bar, and neither knows the other asked it, and a woman of about thirty-four has told three people three different nothings, and none of that came from him. FIVE SIXTHS OF IT CAME FROM THE SIX AND THE SIXTH CAME FROM A BAR, and the review of 27 September 2026 made the chapter count, because as delivered it named seven people and then said *all of it came from the six*.** And then the sentence, and it is flat and has no weight and he does not answer it: **"You are the only one of us who is not talking to anybody. Six of them, and you are the seventh, and I am neither, and there is not one other thing in this county that is like that. Every one of the six of them has been asked about by somebody who was not you this week, and not one of them has been asked about by you twice, and I have been asked twice this month by two of the six and I did not know that was what it was until this morning, and I am the one they are going to carry it to and nobody has asked me whether I would. And I do not know whether that is because you have nothing to give us or because you have given it away."** **SHE USED TO COUNT HERSELF IN AND THE REVIEW OF 27 SEPTEMBER 2026 TOOK HER OUT, BECAUSE SHE IS NOT ONE OF THE SIX AND A LINE THAT COUNTS ITS OWN SPEAKER IS A LINE A READER CANNOT CHECK.** She does not finish it and is not going to and goes out and opens the bar and reads four loads off a board with four letters and a stroke. **He is on nothing in this county except the back of a flour bill in a kitchen three miles up a lane, where a man of sixty-three wrote a stranger's name in a hand that is not good because a stranger said he would walk a hedge, and it is the only name he has anywhere and he did not ask for it and cannot get it off.** He says the last of it out loud to one person: the price of the thing he said in a kitchen nine days ago is that he got it and he did not do any of it, and he has not been thanked and is not going to be, and about six people have agreed to be somewhere on a day and he is not going to be in it and he said that in a yard two days ago and neither time it was an ask. **End: nine days became ten and he was not going to make a thing of a day, and he is going down the lane and up a track and over a bridge with one rail on it in the morning to be at it at about the seventh hour, and the last line of the band is a woman of about seventy-four going down the lane at about the seventh hour to do whatever it is she does on that day, at seventy-four, with a stick and a hood, at the pace of a woman of seventy-four, stopping twice and not stopping a third time, and nobody in this county is going to be standing at that bridge before her.** The day in words: seventieth morning, last day of the sixty-seventh week. No panel, no bold, no new money, the four hundred and eighty-five pounds is not named, and 63,959 is not printed.


## VOLUME 07 BATCH 0001 — Chapters 301–310, *The Seams*. **The live block. The block below it, `## VOLUME 06 BATCH 0005`, and everything under that, is archive and is not edited by this phase.** Chapters 1–310 are canon; `outline/series.md` outranks `outline/volume-07.md` and this file. **This is a summary and not a re-narration: one paragraph per chapter, the finding each one carries, the money with its working where the chapter has a figure, and nothing advanced the chapter does not advance.**

**Chapter 301 — The Fifty-First Morning.** Shelf day 176, the second day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-first morning. The figure at the second light is **sixty-three thousand eight hundred and forty-nine**, which is what the plank says after eight rings, and the eight are Chapter 300's own day and are not in this chapter. His own day is four bells and nothing on top of them and a cart at the bar with nine loads on it. A boy of seventeen comes up the lane with a book that can order things and cannot date them, and says the only day-count in eleven villages is a stranger, and that he cannot date the book and has told three people. **The seam is named for the first time in the fiction, in his own head, at the foot of a ladder, while the woman of forty-one is on the third of four rungs with a cloth on her shoulder: the line where one arrangement stops being true and another one starts.** He can see where the bar and the lane meet and he cannot say what either is for; he has known he could do it for about two years, has told nobody, has used it four times alone, and it has never been any use until this morning. He tells nobody, including her, and she does not ask what he is looking at because in twenty-five years she has not asked one person what a single stroke was for. **The beat: he asks *what is the four for*, and she answers in about nine seconds — four is what most days are — and says that being asked is the only thing that has ever been any use to her, and that he did not ask her what the seven was for, because a man who has been here fifty days asks about the one he can get his hand round.** Six things in his head and not a written list, and the sixth is not a thing yet. He goes up the lane before the second bell, and the last scene is a woman of about fifty at a bar counting nine loads off her own board under four letters and a stroke, not asking him anything. No money. The day in words: fifty-first morning, second day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel.

**Chapter 302 — About Eleven People And A Flour Bill.** Shelf day 177, the third day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-second morning. The board stands at **sixty-three thousand eight hundred and fifty-three**. His own day is four bells and a stranger, and the stranger is him, and **the woman of about fifty at the bar read him off her own board in about four seconds without asking his business, which is the first time in this country that being counted has been a courtesy.** Ashgill is the third village up the lane and has about a hundred and ten people in it and has never been in this book. The walk is not happening: the man of about sixty-three is in a field doing a drain and tells him to go to the second house, and does not stop, and does not stop for a stranger. The rota is on the back of a flour bill in a kitchen because there is nowhere else for it. **He sees the join where the eleven names stop being the rota and the flour price begins, and says a version of it out loud, and a woman of about fifty-one doing something else at the churn tells him it is a crease, and laughs, and the laugh is not unkind and it is the first time in this band that anybody has found him ridiculous and he earned it.** The beat: he asks what the walk is for, and the man of sixty-three stops, and answers in about nine seconds, and the answer is ordinary — *so that nobody has to argue about where the grass is* — and there is not one acre of paper about it anywhere and nobody has ever wanted one, and it will be walked in nine days after he is dead because there is nothing about him in it. **End: his father did it and his father's father did it and nobody ever said out loud what it was for, and if a person did not ask then nobody knew, and a thing nobody knows the reason for is a thing that stops when the last one stops.** No money, and a walk is not priced anywhere in this chapter and printing one is the defect the band exists to avoid. The day in words: fifty-second morning, third day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel.

**Chapter 303 — What A Bell Costs, Said Out Loud.** Shelf day 178, the fourth day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-third morning. The board stands at **sixty-three thousand eight hundred and fifty-six**. His own day is four bells, two strangers, and a boundary. He walks the four hundred yards of hedge alone and sees the join twice and it is a place both times. **Resistance: he is PUT ON THE ROTA. Not asked. The man of sixty-three writes his name on the back of a flour bill because a stranger said he would walk the hedge, and Ilyan knows exactly what that is — a name at the foot of a thing is the only part of it anybody can be asked about — and he says the price of it out loud in that kitchen and does not argue with it, and the man of sixty-three is not told and is not a villain and the cost falls on the stranger.** The turn: eleven names and nine who come, and two who have not come in years and have not been taken off. A man of about thirty-eight who counts other people's money for a living, in that kitchen on his own account and not sent for, says they would come, and coming is not the arrangement, and the arrangement is the hedge and needs nobody, and **the bill is the truth about who turns up and is not the truth about the hedge, and those are two different things and one of them has eleven names on it and the other one has none.** The money, said out loud with the working, to people who had to be told: **a bell, hung, with a rope, is six pounds and fifteen; a keeper's year is five pounds and five; the difference is one pound and ten, every year, for as long as somebody is alive to ring it and somebody is paid to ring it.** 31 × 48d = 1,488 ✓; 1,488 + 156 = 1,644d = £6 17s ✓ (the man of thirty-eight's first and wrong correction of the frame); 1,644 − 1,260 = 384d = **£1 12s** ✓; then the correction that is the point of the chapter, 11s = 132d, 1,488 + 132 = 1,620d = £6 15s ✓; 1,620d = £6 15s ✓ and 1,620 − 1,200 = 420d = 35s ✓; 9 × 140 = 1,260d = £5 5s ✓; 1,260 − 1,200 = 60d = 5s ✓; 1,620 − 1,260 = 360d; 360 − 240 = 120d = £1 10s ✓. **THE METAL FIGURE WAS PRINTED AS *one thousand four hundred and forty-eight* AND 384 PENCE AS *one pound and four* UNTIL THE REVIEW OF BATCH 0001, AND BOTH ARE NOW CORRECT, AND THE ADDITION WAS NEVER THE BROKEN PART — 1,488 + 156 is 1,644 and 1,488 + 132 is 1,620 and both totals were always right, and the defect was entirely in the term being added.** **And a man of about sixty-three says the whole of it in about nine words, in his own mouth, and nobody in that kitchen had ever had that comparison made in front of them, and he does not know what to do with money.** End: he is a name on the back of a bill, with a leg and a bad road and a standing of nobody's, going back on the ninth day, having written nothing down. The day in words: fifty-third morning, fourth day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel.

**Chapter 304 — Four Days Up The Lane.** Shelf day 179, the fifth day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-fourth morning and the fourth day of a walk. The figure is **sixty-three thousand eight hundred and sixty-three**, and he has it from a man of about thirty-eight who had been at Coldharrow that same morning on other business, had stood at the foot of the ladder at the second light because a wall with a figure on it is a thing he cannot walk past, and had gone up the lane afterwards in a cart because he was going this way as well, and who said the number out loud in a kitchen in Ashgill without looking at anything and said that it was that morning's and not yesterday's. **THE CARD FOR THIS CHAPTER NAMED A WOMAN OF ABOUT FIFTY-ONE AND A BOY AND A FIGURE FOUR DAYS OLD, AND NONE OF THAT IS IN THE CHAPTER AND NONE OF IT IS IN ANY OTHER CHAPTER, AND THE DELIVERY TOOK THE PLANK AND THE MAN OF THIRTY-EIGHT BECAUSE SIX OTHER CHAPTERS ALREADY HAD THEM AND A SECOND BOARD-KEEPER AT COLDHARROW IS A CANON BREAK; a later writer must not reintroduce it.** His own day is four bells and a debt called in at the fourth house, and **the debt gets up the lane faster than he does, on a man with a scythe's own legs, carrying nine words and answering no questions**, and the lane is the only difference between this country and a road anybody has ever found. A boy of seventeen walks eleven miles to tell him things, including that he cannot date his book and there are eleven places he can read in order and one he cannot, and that the third is the only thing in it he cannot do. **Resistance: he cannot walk it in time and the man of fifty-two has a cart, and the offer is in the air for about four hours across two days and is never mentioned, and when he finally says one sentence it is about the beast's feet in the wet and a stone on the third rise, and he denies the favour twice unasked.** The join is seen twice, at a gate and at a boundary mark cut on a stone by a road, and both times it is a place and not a bargain: **he can see a join anywhere and it means nothing, and a man who can see a join everywhere and understands nothing is a man with no technique at all, and this is the lowest he goes in the volume and it is here on purpose.** The beat: the villages get shorter, and it is arithmetic and not a mystery — a village of about thirty cannot carry nine arrangements, so the arrangements are fewer and bigger and one person is in more than one, and a person in four arrangements cannot stop any of them because every favour has somebody in it who expects it back. A woman of about thirty-four at a gate with a bar she cannot lift alone says nine words about it in passing and goes on to her work. End: a market town with a weighbridge at the end of the street and a man of about seventy beside it with his hands behind his back who does not look up, and the man of fifty-two says, unasked, that in nine counties in nineteen years there was one man in each who was the only person who could do a particular thing, and that in this county there are about four, and that he has never known which four, and that this is going to be the whole of his winter. The day in words: fifty-fourth morning, fifth day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel, and no money except two unit prices named without a product.

**Chapter 305 — The Offer.** Shelf day 180, the sixth day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-fifth morning, the sixth of ten in the market town. **The board at Coldharrow is not stated and the chapter says why in its second sentence: there is no plank at the end of this street and nobody in this market town has ever heard of a board at Coldharrow, and a man of thirty-one did not come four days up a lane to talk about it.** His own day is four bells, a burial, and a fire, and none of the three is anybody's business, and about nine loads have gone over the bridge. The scales are a set of beams on a stone plinth re-cut three times in a hundred years; a man of about seventy has kept them about forty-four years, has not done the sums for about nine years, and will not let anybody else over the bridge; **his daughter of about fifty-eight has done the sums since she was forty-nine, does them in her head while doing four other things, and is expecting a child in the spring.** No office, no bench, no seat, no chair, no vote, no meeting, no officer, no fund, no wage, no form and no day in any of it, and four hundred loads a week. **THE OFFER: on the bridge, to about nine people, with about nine loads gone over it, he says out loud for the first time in about two years that there is a line where one arrangement stops being true and another one starts, and that he can see where it is and cannot write it down and cannot show it to anybody, and that he has never said it to a living soul. And the price is announced before the offer: nine people will know in about four seconds and there is nothing in the world that can take a knowing back, and he knew that when he said it, and nobody asked him to.** **She says no before he has finished, in about nine words, and it is the best no in the band: a thing nobody can do is a thing nobody has to pay anybody for.** And the rest of it: if one person in a market can do it, then the day he is not there is a day with no scales and four hundred loads a week go over somebody else's guess; and she has a child coming and will be stood up at the spring instead of doing the sums; and he made his offer to a market and not to her, and in a week there will be a man in a tavern saying there is a man on the bridge who can see a join, and in a month somebody will be standing on it waiting for him, and that is not a market, that is a queue. **The seam is real and small and it is no use: he can see where the arrangement stops being a father and a daughter and starts being a market, and he cannot say what either side is for, and the chapter does not let it be a victory.** The father, who does not turn round, says the people of that town call the two of them on a market morning an anchor, and an anchor is not a thing, it is the plinth, the day and the two of them, and it is not a relic and it is not in a box and there is nothing to find. End: he does not apologise and she does not ask him to; about nine people in that town know something about him that had not been true at breakfast; and the last line is his, and it is small, and it is the sentence the volume is built on — he has been in this country fifty-five days and has found out what he is, and it is not that he can see a join. **Money: none. A weighbridge has no wage in the table, and the absence is the chapter, and if you want to price the scales you will have to ask her, and she will tell you there is no price because there has never been a price, which is a sentence and not a figure.** The day in words: fifty-fifth morning, sixth day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel.

**Chapter 306 — Nine People Know.** Shelf day 181, the seventh and last day of the sixty-fifth week, his fifty-sixth morning, **and the day at the bottom end of the lane, which he had been at five days before and not eleven, which is the correction a review of this batch made to `306:5`, the third day reference in the band that named no week and was wrong**, coming down the lane on a cart. **The board at Coldharrow is not stated. His own day is four bells and one more that is on nobody's list, and he never finds out what the one more was, and the woman of forty-one knew by the second bell and was never going to tell him and nobody was ever going to ask her.** The cost of having offered something: on the first morning the town knew, because he said nine people would know and the ninth told two others before supper; by that same evening there was a version of it larger than what he said — *he can tell you what a thing is hiding and he has not charged anybody* — which he wrote down in his own head so that it could not grow, because no instrument in four hundred miles can put the right one back. **On the morning he left, which is the morning after the offer and not the second morning after it, two men had come up the lane and gone back down it, and they overtook his cart about two miles above the bar and told him they had gone to her straight away, before they came down, because she is the one people ask, and she said it was a wet road, and there is nothing to have, because there is no use in a thing that is not a day.** And the finding nobody will ever know: **she has now said no to a whole market instead of to nine people, in a street, in daylight, alone, and nobody thanked her, and the price of that is the price of everything in this book, which is that nobody finds out.** The paragraph that plants the volume's hearing, in the mouth of a man of fifty-two, in one paragraph, said once: a district under a corridor cannot be the scene of a hearing about its own standing, and so a place under a corridor has to send somebody, and the somebody has no standing either, and he has been the somebody in nine counties in nineteen years and has never once been asked whether he would go and has gone every time. **The beat: he says out loud that nobody has ever asked him what he is the only person in, and is asked what it was, and does not answer and does not refuse, and says it is a different road and a longer one, and about half a mile goes by.** End: he is a stranger with a bad leg, a name on a bill, a man who has been told no by a woman of fifty-eight and not forgiven and not condemned. Nobody is relieved. The day in words: fifty-sixth morning, last day of the sixty-fifth week. No panel, no money, and the offer is not restaged as a document and nothing is produced.

**Chapter 307 — The Ninth In The Line.** Shelf day 182, the first day of the sixty-sixth week, his fifty-seventh morning, eleven miles down the lane and off it.
